_meta.purpose: The v0.4.0 Day 1 engines (approved by the Principal on 2026-10-16: D-10, D-12, D-14 (e), D-21, D-26 (c), D-45, D-59): four LLM seats (gpt-oss-120b, its abliterated twin, GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731) and three always-resident companions (the router on the iGPU, the Qwen3 4B embedder and reranker on the CPU), in CONVENTIONS.md §8 order (ATLAS_FRAMEWORK_REVIEW.md Sections 4.1, 4.3, 5.1, 5.3). The gpt-oss-120b-abliterated entry is the v0.3.5 one, unchanged by this revision. Read by phase2/engine-env.py, phase2/04-memory.sh, phase3-models.sh and the orchestrator's Engine Arbiter. The top-level `phased` list records the approved engines that come after Day 1 (phased_rule); nothing reads it.
_meta.pin_rule: llama.cpp build tag b11474, commit b9acf138a1e28ce1fc23b5a4fc4b12444b50f7ea (2026-10-07, CMake version 0.6.0; verified by git fetch on 2026-10-16; S-01). The old pin v0.4.1 (commit b29c606e28a01b1bc8c1351026a0fa6e616bf6c4, build b10964) is built beside it only for the output-parity test (S-02, V25), which covers gpt-oss-120b, deepseek-v4-flash and the router; not glm-5.3-flash (glm5-next and the glm5v projector exist only from b11279, so v0.4.1 cannot load it), nor the Qwen3 embedder and reranker (no next-token logits; T-15 checks them at the pin), nor the unchanged abliterated entry (loadtest.py parity_coverage). Each entry's min_llama_cpp_tag is the first build carrying its architecture (git tag --contains, research_notes/ATLAS v0.4.0 build record/engine_data.md); b11474 satisfies every one.
_meta.port_rule: port = LLAMA_PORT_BASE + index, index 1..20 in list order (S-33; CONVENTIONS.md §8: 8101..8120, config.py ENGINE_PORT_SLOTS). The Day 1 set uses 8101..8107: gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-120b-abliterated keep 8101 and 8102, glm-5.3-flash is 8103, deepseek-v4-flash 8104, and v0.3.5's router, embedder and reranker ports (8108, 8109, 8110) become 8105, 8106 and 8107. A phased engine is appended after index 7, so no Day 1 port moves. The port field below is the value for LLAMA_PORT_BASE=8100; engine-env.py recomputes it from the live setting.
_meta.ctx_rule: ctx_size is the TOTAL KV pool split across slots (llama-cpp-vulkan research §0.7: n_ctx_seq = n_ctx / n_parallel). ctx_per_slot is informational and must not exceed the model's n_ctx_train, which bounds the slot (server-context.cpp n_ctx_slot at b11474): glm-5.3-flash and deepseek-v4-flash 1,048,576, gpt-oss-120b 131,072, the router 262,144, the Qwen3 pair 40,960. Research conflict 9.
_meta.files_rule: files[] names every file the unit loads (model shards and any mmproj) by its repo path, with bytes and sha256 exactly as the Hugging Face tree API (lfs.size, lfs.oid) gave them on 2026-10-16 (research_notes/ATLAS v0.4.0 build record/engine_data.md; D-31). The Arbiter budgets the sum of files[].bytes (config.py EngineSpec.footprint_bytes); footprint_gb is the same total in decimal GB, kept for people, and is read as GiB only for an entry with no byte counts (the unchanged abliterated entry). A set mmproj must also be listed in files[]. Every hash is re-read from https://huggingface.co/api/models/<repo>/tree/main[/<subdir>] at pull time and recorded in <models>/<key>/MANIFEST.json (gguf-models.md §0, §11.1, §12 item 7). verify=research-snippet: the pinned hash is compared with the tree API and a mismatch stops the pull before any byte moves (phase3-models.sh); verify=unverified: the tree-API hash is used alone. A file at the repo root of an entry with a subdir is named without the subdir prefix (glm-5.3-flash's mmproj-F16.gguf), so the pull lists the repo root for it as well as the subdir.
_meta.enumerate_rule: When files[] is empty, the pull step lists the tree (subdir when set) and takes every LFS entry whose basename matches enumerate_pattern (fnmatch, case-insensitive). model_file_pattern selects the file passed to --model (first shard); for single-file models it equals the file name.
_meta.layout_rule: Every file lands flat in $ATLAS_SRV/models/<key>/<basename> (shards must share a directory for llama.cpp to find them, and the mmproj sits beside them). join_into names a file that the pull step must cat-join from files[] in order (raw byte splits, gguf-models.md §8) and whose size must equal the sum of the parts; no Day 1 entry uses it (Meditron-70B, the only one, is retired, S-11).
_meta.kv_rule: kv_class is the Section 4.3 setting under D-29 option (a), approved 2026-10-16 (S-18): f16 where the cache is cheap (glm-5.3-flash 19,712 B/token, provisional until T-04; deepseek-v4-flash 6,880 B/token), q8_0 elsewhere (gpt-oss-120b, the router, the Qwen3 pair), q4_0 on no new entry (only the unchanged gpt-oss-120b-abliterated entry keeps it). engine-env.py renders --flash-attn on with identical --cache-type-k and --cache-type-v for every kv_class but none. kv_types_must_match marks an architecture that refuses different K and V types (MLA glm5-next and deepseek4, src/llama-context.cpp:3907-3910 at b11474). kv_ladder (Apex engine only) is the Phase 3 procedure of kv_ladder_rule; its winning type is written to $ATLAS_ETC/engines/overrides.json and engine-env.py re-renders the env file (gguf-models.md §6, §12 item 2).
_meta.kv_ladder_rule: Contract for phase3/loadtest.py ladder_engine (S-42, D-29 option (a), approved 2026-10-16; replaces v0.3.5's descent to a q4_0 target): the ladder keeps the HIGHEST-precision coherent rung that fits the target context. (1) Rungs are tried in list order, f16 then q8_0; q4_0 is never a rung. (2) f16 is loaded first at the entry's own ctx_size and parallel; when it loads, prints its kv proof lines and answers the coherence prompt it stands, nothing is written to overrides.json and V4 records 'f16 applied and coherent'. (3) q8_0 is tried only when f16 fails to load (refused type, OOM, DeviceLost) or loads incoherent; a coherent q8_0 is written to overrides.json and V4 passes with that note. (4) No coherent rung: V4 and V22 deferred (R19), overrides cleared. There is no ctx_size_f16_cap: the f16 rung runs the whole 131,072-token pool (0.84 GiB of f16 KV by the Arbiter's model). The ladder result is printed in the Phase 3 gate table; it is the document's own procedure, not a baseline_deviation.
_meta.parallel_rule: parallel is the explicit --parallel (never auto: gguf-models.md §1.3; --kv-unified stays off when it is explicit). S-22 (v0.4.0): the standing co-resident profile of S52 (parallel_coresident, ctx_size_coresident) went with the pairing it served (D-32 option (a): one LLM seat resident at a time); no entry carries those keys. glm-5.3-flash keeps 8 slots x 32,768 without --kv-unified (no assertion at b11474 requires it for glm5-next; D-48 sets each engine's slot profile from the Phase 3 kv-estimates measurement and T-04). deepseek-v4-flash runs 1 slot x 131,072 (the stated default; the Principal's context target is a to-do, research_notes/ATLAS v0.4.0 build record/answers.md §2.4).
_meta.placement_rule: placement is gpu (the default: the iGPU, on mem_info_gtt_used) or cpu (D-14 option (e), approved 2026-10-16; research_notes/ATLAS v0.4.0 build record/answers.md §2): embed-qwen3-4b and rerank-qwen3-4b run on the CPU, where they hold host RAM the GTT counter never shows. engine-env.py renders --device none for a cpu entry and omits --n-gpu-layers; the Arbiter charges a cpu entry as the host resident set (its unit's VmRSS, never below its weights' bytes, else its projection; atlas/arbiter.py). Only arbiter_class resident may be cpu (config.py PLACEMENTS).
_meta.decode_rule: D-33 option (c), approved 2026-10-16 (S-25, B-04, B-06), with the floors the Principal approved on 2026-10-17 (D-33, D-47; research_notes/ATLAS open inputs 2026-10-17/recommendations.json): expected_decode_tok_s is null on every Day 1 entry, so V10 never fails a quality-first file on speed against a band nobody has measured on the PRO 495. projected_decode_tok_s is the research projection [low, high] in tok/s (a single figure is written [x, x]), recorded beside the measured rate in the V10 row and never a verdict; projected_decode_source names it. decode_floor_tok_s is the seat's absolute decode floor in tok/s, a positive number. Floors are stated at 8k context and judged on the slower of the 512 and 8k decode points: gpt-oss-120b 25, glm-5.3-flash 6, deepseek-v4-flash 4 (the deep-tier floor of D-47, for whichever engine holds the Apex synthesis role) and router-qwen3.5-4b 20 (judged at V10a, Phase 2). Only the absolute floor fails V10; a fail on glm-5.3-flash or the Apex defers that seat through its V22 row, and its seats fall back to gpt-oss-120b (D-40). A review line at 70% of the projection's low end raises a to-do and never fails. prefill_floor_tok_s is the prefill floor in tok/s at 8k, judged on the 8k prefill point: gpt-oss-120b 200, glm-5.3-flash 40, deepseek-v4-flash 40; none for the router. A seat with no floor (the field null or absent) is recorded only (to-do decode-floors). The unchanged gpt-oss-120b-abliterated entry carries no floor field and keeps its v0.3.5 band and rule. glm-5.3-flash is a post-pin architecture and gets a deferrable V22-style row (D-33 (c)).
_meta.extra_args_rule: extra_args tokens are passed verbatim after the generated flags; no token may contain whitespace, a quote of either kind or a backslash, because systemd splits an unquoted $ARGS at whitespace WITH quotes respected and then removed (systemd.service(5), 'Command lines'), so a JSON token would lose its double quotes (engine-env.py enforces this). --reasoning-format is not passed: its default is auto (VERIFIED) and only none|deepseek|deepseek-legacy are verified as explicit values. Sampling is each vendor's (research_notes/ATLAS v0.4.0 build record/engine_data.md): GLM-5.3-Flash temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95; DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, with --reasoning on and --reasoning-effort high because its chat template defaults thinking off; gpt-oss-120b temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0. Reserved flags are REFUSED by engine-env.py whatever engines.json says (fix round hardening, Section 16.3 item 8 / CONVENTIONS §8 bind; fix round 2 adds every flag that loads a file or opens a network path): --host --port -m --model -mu --model-url -hf -hfr --hf-repo -hfd -hfrd --hf-repo-draft -hff --hf-file -hfv -hfrv --hf-repo-v -hffv --hf-file-v --hf-token --api-key --api-key-file --slot-save-path --mmproj --mmproj-url --ssl-key-file --ssl-cert-file --webui --no-webui --alias -a --api-prefix --rpc -md --model-draft --models-dir --models-preset --path --lora --lora-scaled --control-vector --control-vector-scaled --control-vector-layer-range --chat-template-file --log-file; v0.4.0 adds the options both pins accept that load a file, pull a model, open a network path, run a tool or move the device list (re-read in common/arg.cpp at b11474, S-01): --spec-draft-model --spec-draft-hf -hft -dr --docker-repo -mmu --ui --no-ui --ui-config-file --webui-config-file --ui-mcp-proxy --webui-mcp-proxy --tools --tools-runtime -ag --agent --mcp-servers-config --mcp-servers-json --media-path --log-prompts-dir --video-ffmpeg-dir --grammar-file -jf --json-schema-file -lcs --lookup-cache-static -lcd --lookup-cache-dynamic --device -dev; and the prompt-cache cap --cache-ram -cram, which only cache_ram_mib sets (B-33, approved 2026-10-17; cache_ram_rule) (engine-env.py RESERVED_FLAGS, also in the --flag=value spelling). A token that names LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE is refused too (D-16; env_rule).
_meta.env_rule: env is a map of extra KEY=VALUE lines written verbatim into the engine env file for options whose value cannot travel through $ARGS (JSON). Every LLAMA_ARG_* variable is honoured by llama-server itself, applied before argv (common/arg.cpp 787-811 at b11474; research_notes/ATLAS v0.4.0 build record/pin_facts.md). Values may contain double quotes but not single quotes, backslashes or newlines. Reserved names are REFUSED by engine-env.py (fix round hardening; v0.4.0 re-read every name in common/arg.cpp at b11474, S-01): LLAMA_ARG_HOST LLAMA_ARG_PORT LLAMA_ARG_MODEL LLAMA_ARG_MMPROJ LLAMA_ARG_HF_REPO LLAMA_ARG_HF_FILE LLAMA_ARG_MODEL_URL LLAMA_ARG_API_KEY_FILE LLAMA_ARG_SSL_KEY_FILE LLAMA_ARG_SSL_CERT_FILE LLAMA_ARG_ALIAS LLAMA_ARG_API_PREFIX LLAMA_ARG_RPC LLAMA_ARG_MODELS_DIR LLAMA_ARG_MODELS_PRESET LLAMA_ARG_STATIC_PATH LLAMA_ARG_CHAT_TEMPLATE_FILE LLAMA_ARG_LOG_FILE LLAMA_ARG_SPEC_DRAFT_MODEL LLAMA_ARG_SPEC_DRAFT_HF_REPO LLAMA_ARG_DOCKER_REPO LLAMA_ARG_MMPROJ_URL LLAMA_ARG_UI LLAMA_ARG_UI_CONFIG LLAMA_ARG_UI_CONFIG_FILE LLAMA_ARG_UI_MCP_PROXY LLAMA_ARG_TOOLS LLAMA_ARG_TOOLS_RUNTIME LLAMA_ARG_AGENT LLAMA_ARG_MCP_SERVERS_CONFIG LLAMA_ARG_MCP_SERVERS_JSON LLAMA_ARG_VIDEO_FFMPEG_DIR LLAMA_ARG_DEVICE LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_RAM (the prompt-cache cap, cache_ram_rule); and, defensively, names no env variable has at either pin (refusing a name llama-server never reads costs nothing): LLAMA_ARG_HF_TOKEN LLAMA_ARG_API_KEY LLAMA_ARG_WEBUI LLAMA_ARG_MODEL_DRAFT LLAMA_ARG_SLOT_SAVE_PATH LLAMA_ARG_LORA LLAMA_ARG_CONTROL_VECTOR (engine-env.py RESERVED_ENV). Process variables outside the LLAMA_ARG_* set are refused by name, as an env key and inside any extra_args token (engine-env.py RESERVED_PROCESS_ENV): LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE (D-16, approved 2026-10-17), which turns off the Hadamard rotation of every quantised KV cache at b11474 (src/llama-kv-cache.cpp:315-318, VERIFIED). A quantised cache without the rotation is the dangerous case: without it a q8_0 cache cost gpt-oss-20b 6.2 AIME25 points (31.7% against 37.9% at f16, 37.1% with the rotation; llama.cpp PR #21038).
_meta.cache_ram_rule: cache_ram_mib is each engine's host-RAM prompt-cache cap in MiB, rendered by engine-env.py as an explicit --cache-ram on every engine (B-33; research_notes/ATLAS v0.4.0 build record/answers.md §1.5 measure 5, approved by the Principal on 2026-10-17). It must be an integer of 0 or more, and 0 disables the cache; -1 (no limit) and every other value are refused. When the field is absent the mode default applies: 4096 for chat and vision, 0 for embedding and reranking (engine-env.py CACHE_RAM_DEFAULT_MIB); a mode with no default must carry the field. Set explicitly: the router 1024, the embedder and reranker 0. The seats (gpt-oss-120b, glm-5.3-flash, deepseek-v4-flash) and the unchanged abliterated entry take the chat or vision default, 4096. Without the flag llama-server keeps up to 8192 MiB per server (common/common.h:638 at b11474; -cram/--cache-ram and LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_RAM at common/arg.cpp:1719-1725; VERIFIED), fed with every idle slot at each new task (--cache-idle-slots on), outside the GTT counter and the Arbiter's budget: up to 16 GiB for the router and one seat, the whole host reserve. With these caps the worst case is 5 GiB (1024 + 4096 MiB; INFERRED from the flag semantics). --cache-ram, -cram and LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_RAM are reserved (extra_args_rule, env_rule), so only this field sets the cap. Phase 3 measures each chat server's prompt cache and checkpoints and raises the to-do cache-ram if a cap should change (phase3/loadtest.py).
_meta.slot_rule: --slot-save-path is Appendix B's /srv/atlas/data/slots ($ATLAS_SRV/data/slots), ONE directory for every chat/vision engine; slot files are namespaced by the orchestrator's file names, not by per-engine subdirectories. Saving and restoring slots across swaps is phased after Day 1 (D-44, S-35, T-13).
_meta.licence_rule: licence is the identifier on the model card's front matter and in the GGUF general.license, read on 2026-10-16 and accepted with its engine (S-27; D-34 option (b), D-35 option (a)): GLM-5.3-Flash MIT, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 MIT, gpt-oss-120b Apache 2.0, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3-Embedding-4B and Qwen3-Reranker-4B Apache 2.0. The phased engines carry theirs in `phased`.
_meta.baseline_deviation_rule: A `baseline_deviation` field on an engine records a setting that departs from a CLOSED value in ATLAS_FRAMEWORK_REVIEW.md (the document wins over every script, CONVENTIONS preamble). Contract: phase3/loadtest.py prints every engine's baseline_deviation in the Phase 3 gate table and README.md lists them under 'Baseline deviations', so the Principal sees each one in the printed table, never only in this file. Engines without the field run the closed setting. As of v0.4.0 NO engine carries the field: the Day 1 settings are the approved v0.4.0 values, and the Apex KV ladder outcome is printed from the ladder itself, not from this field.
_meta.phased_rule: `phased` records the engines approved for after Day 1 (D-26 option (c)): the specialist seats Intern-S1 (science), Ling-3.0-flash-Fin (finance) and Baichuan-M3 (medical cross-check), and the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Nemotron 3 Super pulls. Two entries left the list on 2026-10-17, when the Principal approved D-19 (c) and D-60 (b) (research_notes/ATLAS open inputs 2026-10-17/recommendations.json): Qwen3-Coder-Next is not pulled, because there is no dedicated coder seat and GLM-5.3-Flash codes (provisional until the T-03 coding set; it would reopen only on a coding time ceiling GLM misses, an independent fixed-harness score within about 5 points of GLM, or a new coder of 70B or more that fits and beats GLM); EmbeddingGemma 2 is dropped to the watch-list (Section 15.5). A Qwen3-VL-Embedding media index is recorded, not built: it becomes its own item only if the Principal wants photo, screenshot, scan or video search, after Day 1, T-15 and a media corpus. Record only: no script reads the list, nothing is pulled, rendered or loaded from it, and no persona, route or preset names a planned_key. An engine leaves the list by being appended to engines[] after index 7, with its files[], its KV figures (kv_bytes_per_token_f16, kv_state_bytes_per_sequence) and a Phase 3 load test. Where a persona's D-40 runner-up is phased, its Day 1 fallback_engine is gpt-oss-120b and the entry here names the seat it would carry (planned_fallback_for). Phased with no entry here: the drafters (DSpark, MTP heads; D-61), the speech, image and OCR companions (C-04, C-05, C-09 to C-11), slot save and restore (S-35), swap batching (D-23, D-39) and the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash trial (D-46, evaluation only, outside the routed roster).

engines.notes: Pull only the UD-IQ4_XS/ folder (5 shards, 156,822,111,200 B = 146.05 GiB) and the root-level mmproj-F16.gguf (1,128,047,296 B, glm5v projector, 564M parameters; F16 rather than BF16 on Vulkan); never the Shard_Rewrite/*.gguf_file duplicates. Weights and mmproj together are 157,950,158,496 B = 147.10 GiB. KV (llama_memory_hybrid_idx): 11 DSA layers with a K-only MLA cache plus an indexer cache, 19,712 B/token at f16 (0.60 GiB per 32K), so the load log carries two llama_kv_cache size lines (kv_proof_lines 2) and one recurrent line; the 34 KDA layers hold 152,633,344 B of f32 state per slot. Vision on this unit (D-20, S-10) costs no swap while GLM is resident; an image is at most 8,000 tokens plus 2 markers (image_max_pixels 6,272,000, patch 14, merge 2). With the mmproj loaded the server turns context shift off. The embedded NextN (MTP) head loads only with --spec-type draft-mtp, phased (D-61). Sampling per zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash generation_config.json; the template's reasoning_effort defaults to max.

Native dimension 2560: the client truncates each vector to 1024 (Matryoshka) and re-normalises it, and adds the 'Instruct: ...\nQuery:' prefix to queries only (S-41, atlas/memory.py). cache_ram_mib 0 (rendered as --cache-ram 0, cache_ram_rule): no prompt cache on a companion. /v1/embeddings.

external.display_name: Chatterbox 0.1.7 (ResembleAI/chatterbox, CPU, in-process) — character and cloning TTS
external.role: Section 14.1 character and cloning tier: the Alaric and Gideon clones (Section 14.3, V7); loaded inside phase2/voice_render.py and the orchestrator's voice path, never a llama-server unit
external.notes: Section 4.2: 'every load ... of any weight-bearing process ... Chatterbox when invoked' passes through the Arbiter. Class external = the Arbiter grants/queues/refuses the load against the live budget (rule 2), never counts it against the LLM-seat limit (rule 3, D-32: a TTS render must not evict the seat), evicts LRU victims for it only when the budget needs their memory (rule 5 per victim) and holds its footprint in the ledger (rules 1, 9), but starts and stops nothing: the caller runs the process in /opt/atlas/venv-voice (phase2/voice_render.py clone-batch; the orchestrator's voice path) and POSTs /arbiter/load {engine: chatterbox} before and /arbiter/unload after; a 404 from either route means the running orchestrator does not read this list and the caller FAILS, it never skips. footprint_gb 4 is the planning figure (voice-stt.md section 7: ~2-4 GB while loaded); phase2/05-voice.sh registers the measured peak RSS (CHATTERBOX_FOOTPRINT_BYTES) through POST /arbiter/register on every run, which replaces it. Listed under `external`, not `engines`: no port (the CONVENTIONS.md section 8 port rule counts engines[] only), no hf_repo/files (the weights are the HF cache phase2/05-voice.sh fills, HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 afterwards), no llama-server@ unit, no sudoers line (phase2/01-llama.sh writes one per engines[] entry) and no env file (phase2/engine-env.py renders engines[] only). Release (Section 4.2 rule 5, with the right counter for a CPU process; fix round 6): not observable on the GTT counter, so the caller passes its process pid in POST /arbiter/unload and the Arbiter polls /proc/<pid> until the process is gone or its RSS is back (bounded; a timeout leaves the engine charged and is retried by the caller); an unload without a pid is accepted on the caller's word and marked 'not measured'. An external resident is never an eviction victim: a load that needs its memory is queued until the caller unloads. It is not an LLM seat, so seat exclusivity (rule 7) neither evicts it nor queues a seat behind it: only the budget does (v0.4.0; in v0.3.5 an Apex request queued behind it). The move to Chatterbox Turbo and Multilingual V3 is phased behind T-23 (C-09).
